newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Human rights flouted in Zaire, Amnesty says.
newsitem.headline: Human rights flouted in Zaire, Amnesty says.

text.p: Zairean soldiers and Tutsi-led rebels have arbitrarily killed local people and Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire and human rights in the country are being increasingly flouted, Amnesty International said on Friday.
Herve Berger, deputy secretary general of the human rights organisation, told a news conference at the end of a two-week trip to Zaire: "The human rights situation is continuing to get worse."
He expressed concern about the nomination of General Baramoto Kpama Kata, former head of the feared civil guard, as armed forces chief of staff.

"Zairean authorities have created a climate of intimidation, where questions demanding the truth about the role of the authorities in the current crisis are repressed," he said, adding that Amnesty had received reports of killings, rape and pillaging by members of Zaire's army.

He denounced what he called hundreds of extrajudicial killings. "We have received reports about the slaughter of hundreds of Rwandese refugees and displaced Zaireans by Tutsi-led armed groups last week," he added.
Berger, a Swiss national, said that freedom of expression was not respected in Zaire and that those who spoke out were targeted for torture.
He denounced the existence of secret civil guard and other detention centres.
"People are afraid to talk about recent events such as the persecution of members of Tutsi and Hutu minorities and the role of the Zairean Armed Forces in eastern Zaire," he said.
"The armed groups in Kivu are committing deliberate and arbitrary killings of Zaireans and refugees," he added.
Tutsi-led rebels hold a swathe of eastern Zaire along the borders with Rwanda and Burundi.

Berger's team had talks with the Zairean authorities but they were denied permission to travel to the town of Kisangani about 500 km (300 miles) northwest of the border town of Goma to investigate allegations of rights abuses.

"Reports have been received by the organisation about killings, raping and pillage being carried out by the Zairean Armed Forces, including violent attacks on families including beating and raping women and girls as young as 12 in Kisangani," he said.

In a press release, Amnesty quoted Berger as saying: "Despite the authorities' tight control on travel to the country's trouble spots, reports of killings, torture and arbitrary arrests cannot be silenced."

Berger told the news conference that the authorities were holding dozens of political prisoners in detention centres throughout the capital. They were held without trial or charge and denied visits by lawyers, doctors or family.
